utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. Could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have the door closed. As mentioned already yesterday, we have to continue with the question of witnesses and the question how to proceed during this week. Trial Chamber did not yet decide on the question whether or not to impose sanctions. We are expecting submissions by the Prosecution, and later in the day I think we'll hear whether or whether not senior counsel from the OTP will be here tomorrow or on Thursday. But I think it should be decided and discussed in a balanced way. May I then ask with absolute priority, what about the possible witnesses for Thursday and Friday this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our investigator is in contact with the -- our case manager, and it should be solved during the day whether that witness can come or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you would let us know immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for these efforts. Then we have to be aware that when next week is dedicated primarily to hear video testimony, we can't afford to proceed in the way that we get the proffer the day before or the same day because the cross-examination, no doubt, has to follow immediately. Therefore, we want to remind the Defence that the amended proffers for the video witness for Monday is due Wednesday this week, that's tomorrow. The one for Tuesday, on Thursday. The one for Wednesday, this week Friday. The one for Thursday, Monday next week. And for next Friday, Tuesday next week. Of course, no doubt, we would appreciate if we could have these amended proffers even earlier. Based on the experience that there will be always the one or other gap or even the impossibility to hear a witness by videolink due to bad weather conditions or other conditions we can't influence, we would hereby order the Defence to present and to call two additional witnesses for next week. It would then be the case that we have three remaining weeks and 13 witnesses and two expert witnesses to come. And therefore, we hereby order the Defence to call five witnesses per week. No doubt, there is some discretion in case there would be a cross-examination on experts that then if this would be the last week, and I took it from your statements that the two experts would appear during the last week, that during the last week we could hear three witnesses and two expert witnesses. We had to go in some more details of the defendant's Milomir Stakic motion for leave to introduce written witness statements pursuant to Rule 92 bis. As indicated already yesterday, the first threshold is, no doubt, Rule 73 ter (D) whether or not it's in the interest of justice to have additional witnesses or not. We found that based on this, and this is the overall decision, we would, with the reservation - details will follow - we grant additional or we accept additional witnesses Milan Cuk, that is (a) on page 3; Zorka Cuk, (b); Nada Ratkovic, that's lit (e); Mira Stakic, that's (l); Bozana Stakic, that's lit (m); and as mentioned yesterday, a written statement by Mr. Timothy McFadden from the United Nations Detention Unit. Before ruling on this, I want to ask the Defence on behalf of the Chamber, what about the children of Dr. Stakic? Do you insist or do you want to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. We would withdraw the request for the children to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this protection of the children of Dr. Stakic. I think it's in the sound interest of the children, and we take their testimony in principle as given. Nothing else can be expected from children. All the other remaining witnesses, this is Dr. Slavko Tomic, this is Aleksandar Radakovic, this is Jovan Ratkovic, this is Marija Vukadinovic, this is Miroslav Kamsak, this is Jasminka Kneginjic, this would be more appropriate for Judge Vassylenko, Mr. Milorad Loncar, and Marijana Nikolic, and the other unnamed witnesses we can find on page 3 of Appendix 1 under (p) and (q), they are not admitted as additional witnesses because it's not in the interest of justice to hear these additional witnesses, in part that is what is expected as their testimony is already proven. It would be repetitive. And in part, not relevant for the outcome of this case. So therefore, all in all, it means that we have, based on this list, five additional witnesses admitted. They all are in agreement with the statements of the Prosecution from yesterday. In principle, witnesses whose testimony can be admitted under 92 bis, but as to the fact that the documents provided for us, especially Appendix 1, is not sufficient for a final decision, be it under Rule 73 ter or 92 bis, we have to make the reservation that the admission is only an admission in principle and can always be reversed, and the same is true when we are stating that in principle it can be admissible to hear these five witnesses under Rule 92. Also this decision is subject to a decision to reverse the question of admissibility under 92 bis. The final decision can only be taken when we have the statements as such. In result, it means that during the next week, ten 92 bis statements have to be taken and five video conferences to be conducted for five witnesses. We would appreciate if as soon as possible we could have the calling order for the next three weeks in advance that at least based on the names, we can be prepared what will happen in this courtroom. The next question to be resolved is the translation of exhibits, at least in part. With some concern, we see that a number of translations are still missing. We already several times ago offered our assistance if there would be a problem with the translation, but yesterday we heard that in part, there would be translations available. May I ask, are they already provided to the Prosecution, and would they also be available for the Chamber, those translations already provided by the translation section?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps to clarify the point, I could give the Court just a brief background so that we're discussing the exact same issues, if the Court permits. On November 18th of 2002, the Defence submitted a specific list of exhibits of articles that we requested to be translated. Approximately six weeks thereafter, after the new year, we were asked to highlight specifically which articles it was that the translation unit was to have translated from B/C/S into English. We thought our index was clear enough because it identified by the title of the article that which we requested to be translated. Subsequent to that, we did highlight the sections which we requested, and we were returned approximately two fifths of the documents that we requested. We then submitted that to the OTP and to the Chamber of the documents that were translated. Since that time, we have requested orally and I believe once in writing that they continue to advise us as to the status of the translation. We have not completed -- or they have not completed that task, and we are still awaiting the completed translation of all the Defence exhibits as forwarded on November 18th, 2002. We are asking to the extent it's possible for this Chamber somehow to assist the Defence in expediting that translation. We're unaware of the specific procedure outside of asking for an order compelling them to translate it by a certain given date. So once again, that's the status. We don't have the documents completely translated. Those that have been translated have been forwarded to the OTP and to the Chamber. And we're still awaiting any day for the balance of the documents to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a little concerned because we don't have any recollection of receiving any documents, and I don't trust my own recollection but Ms. Karper tells me we haven't received any documents. Obviously, this is a problem that could delay the whole case, and I think I would encourage the Court or ask the Court to contact CLSS and find out what is the problem with these translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We received -- the Chamber received a stack of documents, but only in part translated. Based on the experience, and this is one of the flaws in this Tribunal, a number of documents are translated and then never used in Court. For the reputation of this Tribunal, I don't want to give figures how many documents being translated and then later not used in Court. Therefore, being relatively close to the end of the Defence case, I would invite the Defence, if possible, to concentrate on those documents Defence really wants to use in Court. But I asked several times in the past who is the person responsible for this work, who is your contact point?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We hesitate to always identify that person, Your Honour, for fear of any retribution against them, but our contact quite frankly was through the Registrar's office and a gentleman by the name of Laurent Wastelain was the person with whom we continued to and have consistently since November, he has been our intermediary. In essence, we have given him the list, have made the request through him, and he has gotten back to us with, as I mentioned, the issue of highlighting articles. And when the translation was completed he was the individual who transferred that to us. So he is our only contact. We don't have contact specifically with anyone at the translation department. The gentleman has been working and has been cooperating with us. I must say he has been extremely helpful. It is not his specific department I gather in the hierarchy. So I hate to say that it's his fault and I don't want to suggest that it is. It is my understanding yesterday, Mr. Laurent Wastelain was in not in the office and I'm not sure if today he is here because yesterday it was my understanding that he was taken ill. So although we tried calling his office yesterday, that was the information that we obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we are all aware that there is a hierarchy, but we need the first point of contact that we can continue. We'll try and assist you and find out what is possible. But I think there was also an offer from the side of the Prosecution related to some documents when identifying the 65 ter number. Based on this, maybe the translation is already available from the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Karper identified for the Defence the translations that were already done. So that was provided -- CLSS says there are some. We can provide that. There are some that are already translated. We can make sure that CLSS has that. They should have that already. But we'll make sure that the Defence has that to give to CLSS. But I would reiterate, since we received the 65 ter set of documents which I think were almost all untranslated, I don't know if there were any translations in there, we have not received any documents. There may be some misunderstanding. We have not received a set of translations. We have received nothing since November or December when the original 65 ter list was provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe there was then a mistake because to the best of my recollection, we are all bad witnesses, as we know. We received in any event 100 or 200 pages at the beginning of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will certainly take the request and follow up on in. Mr. Cirkovic our case manager is the one who advised me that it was distributed to the Chamber and the OTP. To the extent that it was not, or even if it was, we will provide them with another copy as soon as practical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I would invite the parties to get in contact and to find out. Maybe in other cases, some documents have already been translated, and therefore they can be available without any additional translation. This is another shortcoming in this Tribunal, that apparently some documents are not only translated twice. So please contact and find out where you can be of assistance, mutual assistance, on translation. We will find out what other problems in the CLSS. One additional problem is for the Trial Chamber how to introduce the results of the CD-ROM tendered by the Defence, admitted into evidence, and then it was only yesterday that we received the figures and the result what we can find out based on this CD-ROM. We are hesitant to order during the Defence case the Prosecution to give a summary or affidavit of the person who provided these figures. On the other hand, from our understanding of general principles in criminal law and in criminal procedure, it seems to be extremely difficult to order the Defence to produce evidence because from our point of view, we never know whether this could be of self-incriminatory nature or not. Therefore we would be absolute hesitant save the Defence would state, We believe this is a reliable source and we believe that we can live with the outcome of figures here and we can't just introduce the figures. Of course, we would need an affidavit. Therefore, it would be the question whether first the Prosecution would be prepared to give such an affidavit. We would not order this. And then it would be for the Defence to answer the question whether or not they are prepared to accept this summary of the results of the figures to be found on this CD-ROM. May I please first hear the Prosecution on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, an affidavit has been drafted at my request. I asked for a few changes for the person who prepared it to explain his own background a bit. It's about a page long, and it should be ready today. My suggestion is the Defence can look at it. If they want to put it into evidence or they want to admit it by stipulation, we would agree. If not, the Court could order it produced by the Prosecution under Rule 98 or we could 98 bis it for our rebuttal, if that would be of assistance. Whatever procedure is agreeable to the Defence and the Court. We could 92 bis the affidavit in our rebuttal case if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt we would appreciate to have these figures in evidence as soon as possible. What is the submission by the Defence related to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We would like to naturally first see the affidavit, and then we would like to do our own verification on the numbers. And the question we have is the three categorisations within that exhibit if it actually comports with what's on the CD-ROM. And specifically we would like to just mention that it's the testimony of the witness Mrs. Kovacevic who brought the CD which we think it's important to classify that last third category. The question unfortunately is not when the OTP think certain people became refugees and came to the Prijedor Municipality. Those documents reflect when they registered. So it should be clear, although made in argument, that it does not state as they allege, as they have with other subjective witnesses whether it's Sebire, Inayat, or O'Donnell, it's a question of that these people came prior to the date but only registered on the date that's identified in those exhibits. So again, we would like to reserve the right to examine the affidavit, verify these numbers, and then we would ask the Court, of course, that they take that exhibit consistent with and incorporate it with Mrs. Kovacevic's testimony which I believe, as I've stated in summary, was accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think before the Defence gives a final assessment, you should rethink, because it could be to the disadvantage of your client questioning some of these figures. And I think already during the testimony, we reflected these numbers or these figures in part, and it was to a certain extent agreed by this witness what we saw immediately based on our laptop first perusal that this would be the outcome of this calculation. But I would invite the parties to discuss this affidavit. Maybe you can find another form to introduce this. In this case, no doubt, as it's the Defence case, it would be for the Defence to give additional evidence or additional assessment if they don't believe that those figures we have before us reflect that what can be found on the CD-ROM. And it's a relatively easy exercise. But I expect that this problem be solved during this week. Yesterday, we asked the Prosecution to produce the Official Gazette of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, year 1, number 3, dated Monday, the 16th of March, 1992. We intend to admit these documents under J27. Are there any objections by the parties? Defence, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as J27A and B respectively. May I ask, in order to avoid any kind of misunderstanding, the Defence, do you have any questions related to the order when to provide proffers and when to call witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We had envisioned unfortunately a slightly different schedule than the Court had ordered. Mr. Lukic is leaving Thursday to go to the field in order to meet and prepare with the witnesses. We anticipated that with respect to the first videolink witness, that we would provide the Court and the OTP with the proffer on Friday, and then we anticipated that by no later than Sunday, we would be able to provide the proffers for the balance of the four witnesses who will be giving testimony via videolink. We think it's necessary for one of the attorneys of record to meet with the witnesses so that the proffers are consistent with that which the testimony will be so that again we don't be put in a position to have second-hand information which may be somewhat inaccurate. That has been our plan, to be perfectly candid with Court. We will try and we will endeavour to comply with the Court's order of this morning. It is somewhat taxing for us because we're both here, and Mr. Lukic is planning, as I stated to, leave on Thursday. We have scheduled to meet with these witnesses this weekend so that we should have all the proffers, as I've stated, to the Court no later than Sunday for the balance four. But we hope to give to the OTP and the Court the proffer on Friday for the witness that will testify on Monday via videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Submissions by the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is that Friday morning, may I ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That would be Friday morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could live with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But to be serious, we warned the Defence a number of times, and these proffers we are fighting for now, they are due since December, if not November, last year. And to be honest, we are not prepared to fight on a daily basis for each and any proffer. It's your obligation. And I am more than surprised once again to hear even the proffers for the video witnesses, and we know the names for a long period of time, we had a break of one week for preparation, so we really cannot understand this. Let's put it this way, that based on the submission by the OTP and it's first of all the right of the OTP being more or less the master of all our archives and therefore having the best possible access to the necessary data, if the Prosecution in this exceptional case is prepared to continue, then of course we would not interfere. But it's not satisfactory at all. So let's fix for the video witness of Monday, Friday, 12.00 sharp. But no later than 12.00 sharp. My understanding is that Prosecution can live with this. What about the witness for Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The balance of the proffers will be prepared Sunday afternoon, Your Honour, and would be tendered to the Court and to the OTP Sunday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All the four other video witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And when can we expect the names of the two additional witnesses to be called next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe we can expect that by Thursday of this week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the proffers?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Those proffers will also be tendered by Sunday -- sorry, by Tuesday morning, no later than 12:00 p.m., Your Honour, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the additional two witnesses we have to hear in this courtroom, in addition to the video witnesses, I'm speaking about these two witnesses we have to hear starting from Monday next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understood the question. And we expect the videolink to proceed Monday with the five witnesses to be carried continuously, and then as time permits, we would call those two additional witnesses. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe you misunderstood my remarks, even though I believe it was clear enough. We always have problems with videolinks, and it may be that even already on Monday, a videolink could not be established for the one or other reason. And therefore, it's mandatory that as from Monday afternoon, next week we are sitting in the afternoon shift, as from Monday afternoon we have the first witness available. So it would be for the Defence to call the first witness for Monday, and let's say the second witness for Wednesday. But we need in any event two additional witnesses; otherwise, we would have the same disaster as we have it this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do understand the Court's request now, and thank you for the clarification. We will certainly endeavour to bring the two witnesses here Sunday. Of course, in part, it's out of our hands. We're waiting to get the visas and the transportation arranged. To the extent the Court can assist us with the Victim and Witness Unit to coordinate that and expedite that, we would be in advance grateful for any assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First of all, the prerequisite is that you give us the names, 65 ter numbers, coordinates of this these witnesses as soon as possible. But for the witnesses to come next week as ordered, normally even the amended proffers should be due tomorrow for the witness to come on Monday next week. Therefore unfortunately, I have to take it that nothing has been prepared yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No amended proffers have been prepared, Your Honour. That's correct, Mr. Lukic who was in the field last week, was unfortunately taken ill and was hospitalised or went to the hospital for a day, as I believe he reported to the Chamber through a telephone conversation. So that has unfortunately delayed the process. But to the extent possible, we will endeavour to get the proffer of the witness -- the live witnesses by Friday. And we'll -- again, once we meet with them on Saturday and Sunday, immediately thereafter, we'll notify OTP of any additional comments or statements they may share with us. But it's difficult for us to do that via telephone with the witnesses, and as we have seen in the past, the reliability of third-hand information sometimes is not as helpful as we would like. So to the extent that we can, we will provide an amended proffer, and once we physically meet in person with the witness, we will notify the OTP and the Court immediately of any additional statements or areas the witness wishes to cover consistent with the fourth amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, frankly, I'm a little less concerned with the proffer than getting the names so we can begin our computer search, and that's my main concern. If we can get by tomorrow the names of the possible witnesses for next week, then we can do our computer search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's also our concern, that also the Bench is able to prepare, and when only we have the names, then it's easier to prepare. So therefore, we hereby order the Defence to give us the two names for the live witnesses to come next week no later than tomorrow, 12.00. In order once again to avoid repetitive situations, we want to ask the Defence to give us the names of the witnesses to come for the week from 3 to 7 March no later than Tuesday next week. Names, this is -- this includes dates and place of birth and father's name. Is this agreeable for you? Is it feasible?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will comply with that order, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Prosecution can live with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the same would then be true for the next week, once again, on Tuesday the week in advance at least the names, for the week 10 to 14, and then 17 to 21 March. Anything else which could cause any obstacle or impediment for the ongoing procedures? Please, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I many. Perhaps I'm not understanding the Court's question, but in the invitation generally speaking we expect to have our academic historian testify during the week of March 10th, specifically the 12th, 13th, and 14th if that's the Friday, although I think it might be court maintenance day. That's the schedule we have now envisioned, and we were leaving the last week for our military expert to testify. Again, we're at the Court's obviously discretion how you'd like to proceed. I do note the Court mentioned that you're going to have both experts and three witnesses in the last week. Just to advise the parties that that is our plan now to call, as we have indicated before on the record, that we were going to call Mr. Trifkovic on the week of March 10th, and that's how I scheduled with him. At the Court's instruction, to schedule in advance with the experts, because of their schedule and et cetera. So that's our plan now, if that doesn't work --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, correct. Then we would, say, for the week 10 to 14 March, four witnesses and one expert. I take it that the Prosecution has already indicated that they want to examine both -- cross-examine both experts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We haven't seen the report, but I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It goes without saying. So then for this week, 10 to 14, four witnesses plus one expert witness. And the same would be true, 17 to 21, four witnesses plus one expert witness. Only this schedule allows us to concentrate and this Chamber will additionally work with the time limitations, and therefore please when you provide the amended proffers, be extremely careful because we will take you by your word. If we read the testimony will take you two and a half hours, it will be two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just if we may comment, yesterday we hesitated to just jump on our feet. The Court mentioned with the witness that's on the stand that we had initially stated it was two hours in the amended proffer, but quite candidly the amended proffer states it was going to take four hours. And the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can give you the reason why. Because the amended proffer I had access to my computer, and there we could only find the amended proffer only during the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted it to be clear we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is the reason. And I hope you can understand that we can't continue this way, that we find during the first break the amended proffer because it was sent via e-mail to the Presiding Judge only, and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have the other e-mails. How would -- when we went through the Court officer, the Court instructed that we e-mail it directly to Your Honour so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But please not in this last-minute way. You have read the order. The order clearly states two working days in advance, not last-minute. The e-mail system was checked the last time last Friday, 6.00, and there was nothing available. No amended proffer, to be quite clear. Anything else from the side of the Prosecution also in preparation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Only one clarification, on the Defence list updated the 17th of February, 2003, it reads: "The 65 ter number 025 would be a possible 92 bis witness." Following already our order in writing, and the discussion of yesterday, we decided that this witness has to testify live and not under 92 bis. Therefore, I would kindly ask Madam Registrar to delete the words "92 bis" on the list of comments. If any of the parties identify the one or other maybe mistake, please let us know. We are all aware how difficult it is for Madam Registrar to follow these gallop through the list of witnesses which normally should have been done in November of last year. So I think the time is ripe for cross-examination. I heard yesterday the Prosecution is prepared. May I therefore ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. We would schedule the first break at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prastalo. You are prepared to continue with the cross-examination now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the floor is for Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May ask the usher to move back the ELMO a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You told us that you first met Dr. Stakic when he was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly and liked him immediately, that you socialised with him in 1992, and that again, you socialised with him in Belgrade in more recent times. In page 71, line 10 of yesterday's transcript, you said: "Whenever we had spare time, maybe once, two, three times a month, depending on the extent of our professional activities. Sometimes we would see each other four or five times a month; sometimes once a month depending. Lately, we have been spending more time together." Sir, in all of these contacts you had with Dr. Stakic, you mentioned his interest in business and in his family. Did Dr. Stakic ever express or manifest to you any interest in the well being of the citizens of Prijedor, other than his interest in business and his own family?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you -- can you tell us, for example, you mentioned the tragic shooting of your friend Goran Dragojevic on the 30th of May, the ambulance driver. Did Dr. Stakic express his concern with what happened to Mr. Dragojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, I was not with Dr. Stakic, and I couldn't discuss that with him. It was only after five or ten days that I saw him, and it was not only Dr. Stakic but everybody who knew Mr. Dragojevic, who -- they were all concerned. Dr. Stakic knew him from the workplace, from the place where they worked before all of these events. This man was very professional in his job, and by accident on that day, he had a task to do this humanitarian job. He didn't know what would happen. He set off like every other day to do his job professionally, the job that he did in the health centre. And it was -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic felt very sorry for him, and other people as well felt very sorry for him, not only Serbs, but everybody that Goran socialised with, like I socialised with him. Everybody felt sorry for Goran and for what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic simply express to you that he felt sorry for Mr. Dragojevic, or did he do anything to help Mr. Dragojevic, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dragojevic, as far as I know, was hospitalised in Prijedor. I didn't see Dr. Stakic visiting him. I did go to see what had happened. There was a state of chaos there. All of us who knew Goran went to see what had happened to him. All of us went to the hospital to inquire as to what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And in fact, Mr. Dragojevic was transferred, given medical care not just in Prijedor but in Banja Luka and Belgrade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, did Dr. Stakic trust you even though you were not a member of any political party? Did you feel you had his trust?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask for his trust, trust is something that is built over a long period of time. I never attended any political meetings, attended any negotiations. I was not a member of any political parties. Our conversations had nothing to do with politics. We would discuss my job, we would discuss his life, my private life. We never -- in a manner of speaking, he never interfered with my -- what I did and I never interfered with what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Aside from Mr. Dragojevic, did Dr. Stakic express concern with the well being of the citizens of Prijedor to you in 1992 or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know Dr. Stakic, I know that he didn't feel very comfortable with all that. He experienced hard moments like we all did. I don't distinguish between the president of the Municipal Assembly and a common citizen like I was. We all went through difficult times. Like I said yesterday, we were not in favour of a war against our fellow citizens because we all lived together. And if we people who meant something in the town, we know who was behind all of that, we knew all these people. I knew them personally. So we felt really bad about all that, not only Dr. Stakic, but everybody in the town of Prijedor and in the territory of the municipality. This is a small municipality. We all know each other. We used to work together before the war. As far as I know, Dr. Stakic worked in a village that is about 25 kilometres away from Prijedor. The name of the village is Omarska. Different people came to see him as patients. There were Serbs, there were Muslims. As far as I know, Dr. Stakic was a humanitarian person in his profession. As far as his work in the Municipal Assembly is concerned, I know that he was appointed in the way people are appointed to a position like that. I believe that this was not a good position for him. I think that the best position for him would have been to open a private surgery, but he didn't have the money for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Sir, we won't finish if you continue to answer things that are not related to my question. The question I asked you only related to Dr. Stakic and to whether he expressed any concern for the well being of other people besides Mr. Dragojevic. Can you give the names of any other people in 1992 that you recall Dr. Stakic speaking about and expressing his concern for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't mention any names. I already said that I knew Mr. Dragojevic and Dr. Stakic knew him also. We did not discuss Mr. Dragojevic's case at great length. We just exchanged a few words, and I know that he was very sad. Dr. Stakic was very sad about what happened to Mr. Dragojevic. But we didn't mention any other names because we didn't know at the time who else was killed or injured. I personally know the name of a policeman, an active-duty policeman from the village of Lamovita. He had been killed. I don't know whether Dr. Stakic knew him or not. We never mentioned him in a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I stopped you because you were talking about a policeman you knew and my question was related to what Dr. Stakic said. You said on page 61 of yesterday's transcript: "Dr. Stakic found himself there by mistake." And I understood you to be referring to the position of president of the municipality. Page 61, line 21, you said: "I think Dr. Stakic found himself in that place by mistake." Were you referring to the position of president of the Municipal Assembly, president of the Crisis Staff? Are those the positions that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are talking about Dr. Stakic, I'm talking about him as a person, but I'm not making a distinction between the different positions. I did mention the Crisis Staff, and I know that he was a vice-president of the Municipal Assembly who received me. I can't say that he directly helped me, but he expressed interest in my case. When I say the president of the municipality, I meant the president of the Municipal Assembly. And what I meant was that he is not a person who was -- whose place was in politics. But I believe that he thought that his knowledge, his cool head, and his moderation would result in a normal life in Prijedor. But personally, I know that in our system, the president of the municipality could not make any decision. President of the municipality was a legislative power, and the Executive Board was the executive power. And the president of the municipality could not make any decisions. Decisions were made by the Municipal Assembly, and the president of the assembly in our system --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was a person who --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you to discuss the powers of the president of the Municipal Assembly right now. We will not finish if you get off the -- if you go beyond the questions that I'm asking you. Do you know that Dr. Stakic -- you say he was there by mistake. Did Dr. Stakic put his name forward? Was he on the election as a member of the Municipal Assembly? Did he accept the position of vice-president of the Municipal Assembly? Did he accept the position of vice-president of the SDS? Did he accept the position of president of the Crisis Staff all in 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking at crosspurposes. What I said was that it is my opinion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I wasn't talking about whether you accepted that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is an examination where I ask the questions and, please, if you could just give your best answer to the questions. Did Dr. Stakic accept those positions or are you aware that Dr. Stakic accepting those positions in the 1990 election and in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he accepted that. He accepted as soon as he found himself in these positions. That means that he had accepted the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In 1997, after going through the experiences of 1992, at the end of the war in 1996 or 1997, did Dr. Stakic again put himself forward as president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You don't know if Dr. Stakic was president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor a second time at the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, but I don't know whether he himself put himself forward for that position. I don't know what the procedure is like. But I know that he was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you talked about someone's telling you that Dr. Stakic was not a member of the SDS. Do you know that Dr. Stakic founded a political party, the radical party -- People's Radical of Nikola Pasic? Are you aware of that, before the 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I said that I had heard, and I said who I had heard it from. Jokingly, I asked him about that. I heard that from the people that Dr. Stakic was a member and the founder of that party, the radical party Nikola Pasic -- the main founder was actually Veljko Guberina. Dr. Stakic was on the founding committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Stakic later became the vice-president of the SDS, and when he came back as the president of the municipality a second time, he was again -- it was again a Municipal Assembly controlled by the SDS. He was proposed as a candidate by that party -- excuse me. I'll withdraw the question. You said you were not aware of him coming back as president a second time, so I'll withdraw that question. Sir, in my language we have an expression about someone's membership in a group where we use the expression "card-carrying member." Would you have any explanation -- do you believe that Dr. Stakic was a member of the SDS party from April 30th, 1992, onwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he did not have a party card. Whether he was a member of the party, whether he could have been the president of the Municipal Assembly if he was not a member of the SDS, I don't know. But I know that he was a member of the Nikola Pasic party, and that he became the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly without being a member of the SDS. But a little while ago, we didn't understand each other. I didn't say that I don't know that Dr. Stakic was the president of the Municipal Assembly for the second time. The way I understood your question was whether he himself put himself forward to become the president. That, I don't know. But I do know that he was the president for the second time. So when you say that I didn't know that he was the president of the Municipal Assembly for the second time, that is not correct. What I don't know was whether he put himself forward, whether he volunteered to become the president for the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And I thank you for correcting my misunderstanding. When did you work in 1992 after the 30th of April? What were your working hours during the rest of the spring, summer, and fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My working hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked around the clock. The petrol station was open until 2200 hours, and I travelled all over the place day and night. This had nothing to do with the working hours of the petrol station. It was very difficult to obtain derivatives under those very difficult conditions. One needed to do all sorts of paperwork, customs, clearance, and things like that. So I worked a lot, and I didn't have any specific working hours. When you are a private entrepreneur, you work all sorts of hours. I didn't work for a socially-owned company; I worked for myself. Everything that I did was for myself. I was the one who determined my working hours, and as far as my health served me and as far as I was fit, I travelled at all kinds of hours, all the time, around the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I gather then that when you met with Dr. Stakic and your other friends and played billiards and those things, that would have been after the gas station closed at night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not work at the petrol station. I had workers working there. I was their boss. It was not up to me to be there physically all the time. I had other things to tend to. I also had time off. I had my leisure time. And when we are talking about billiards, I didn't play billiards just with Dr. Stakic. There were other people I socialised with. I said that from time to time, I would also play billiards with Dr. Stakic. When we were both free at the same time. A huge difference was between me and Dr. Stakic, and it laid in the fact that Dr. Stakic had a family in Prijedor and I didn't. My family was in Belgrade so that I spent very little time at home in my parents' house or in my sister's apartment in Prijedor. I was not a family man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would you see Dr. Stakic playing billiards in the middle of the day, the middle of the work day, or would you play billiards with him and see him out during the evening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes we would play during the day; sometimes late in the afternoon; sometimes on weekends we play at different hours. During the working days, from Monday to Friday, we did not play billiards before 2.00 in the afternoon. If we did, we played after 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. Sometimes we also socialised, playing billiards, sometimes we would have a coffee in the evening and a drink around 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening. Again, I would like to say that I socialised with other people, directors of other companies, and this was very closely connected with business interests, if you know what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not asking about your socialising with other people now. When you saw Dr. Stakic, who else would Dr. Stakic be with?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes he was on his own, and very often, he was accompanied by his son. We didn't hang out with a lot of people. There were just a few of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Who were the few of you that hung out together?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic, myself, Mr. Rajko Stupar. There was another young man whose name I don't know. But he played billiards with us quite often. I know his nickname. If you want, I can give you his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I give you his nickname?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Burgija. I don't know what his name is. He's a young man, maybe in his early 30s, around 35 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you ever play --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was not a huge crowd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see Dr. Stakic with Mr. Kovacevic and Mr. Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Kovacevic. He came to me on several occasions to ask for derivatives from my petrol station for the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Did you see Dr. Stakic with Mr. Kovacevic and Mr. Drljaca? I'm not asking you about your relationship with Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see him with Dr. Kovacevic. I didn't see him with Mr. Drljaca. I saw Stakic, Kovacevic, and Drljaca in the same restaurant, but not sitting at the same table. I saw Stakic and Kovacevic sitting at the same table in the restaurant which I often went to take my meals. So I would see Dr. Kovacevic and Stakic together on several occasions sitting at the same table, and at the same time there was Drljaca sitting with some other uniformed men, men belonging to the same profession sitting at a different table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the Kod Pale restaurant?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I went to that restaurant very often. The name of the restaurant is Pale, and it is the name of the owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I wasn't asking you that. Sir, did you socialise with Mr. Budimir and Mr. Travar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you play cards with any members of the Crisis Staff in the Municipal Assembly basement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dr. Stakic go into the Municipal Assembly at night, see him there or did he tell you that he was going there at night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did Mr. Budimir or Mr. Travar ever tell you that they had to go and do a night duty and be at the Municipal Assembly building all during the night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have already said that I didn't discuss their job. When they went there, what they did there, I don't know. I know that Mr. Travar was a member of the Executive Board or what have you. I don't know. But I never discussed that with them, and they were not supposed to account for their doings to me, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit S235-12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This morning, sir, you gave an answer - and I cannot -- I do not have it in front of me right now - regarding I believe you said Dr. Stakic did not have a membership card to the SDS. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it. I've said and I shall repeat it that yesterday in private session, I said that people whom I mentioned yesterday in private session told me that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party Nikola Pasic. Dr. Stakic never showed me his membership card for any party, for the SDS or any, and I never asked him to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this? Does this appear to you to be a membership card for the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, and as far as I can tell, this is an identity card. This is Dr. Stakic's identity card. This is not an SDS party membership card. I've never seen it, though, but this is an identity card.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What about the card that's above the identity card?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It does appear, Your Honours perhaps on the ELMO it is not clear that these are two separate documents that are photocopied on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe we can invite the witness to read what the witness can see on this document that we have it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, the top card, the top rectangular document, can you read out what that says before the exclamation point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we should have the entire document on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Free democratic Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then we can see a broken chain. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then three letters. What are they saying? Is it SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see a chain, and it says here "Serbian democratic party," and it also says "SDS." And underneath that is the identity card. I've never seen this before, nor is this an SDS party membership card. We all had identity cards like this. I have never been a member of any party. I've never seen anything like this before. I don't know what this means. This looks more like a photocopy of an identity card. So these are probably two documents. In the upper right-hand corner, there is a number, 02017201, and this does not correspond to the number at the bottom where it says RS00237577, so these must be two different things. And I am not familiar with any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I think we should treat these as two separate documents. I believe you are correct that these are two separate documents photocopied on the same page. You said that "we all had these." I presume you are referring then to the identity card. You all had identity cards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you have a card that you carried with you like the top rectangular saying -- that has the SDS logo and the name of the Serbian democratic party?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had that. I had what you see in the lower part because that was an ID. But not with the upper part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's an appropriate time for a break, and maybe it's possible to have the underlying documents where these photocopies stems from --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Some of those were the ones returned. We'll try to determine if this is one of the ones that was returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So please find out whether it's possible or not to find the originals. The trial stays adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May I ask the witness to be brought in immediately. Mr. Koumjian, you may proceed. Did you find the originals or is it just a miscopy, to put it this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I believe those are part of the documents that were returned to the Detention Unit, so we do not have the original. And we don't have any other copy other than what the Court has, at least that we have found so far. May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday, on page 36 of the transcript, you were talking about Hidraflex. And you said beginning on page -- line 18, "Since I was speaking about the enterprise, perhaps I should finish. I may leave the time frame we were talking about, but there was something else that was important that happened, too. While I was still down there, I enjoyed the support of the --" and then there's a question in the transcript about what word you used, legally- or illegally-elected government. What was it when you were talking about the Hidraflex company, you said, "I enjoyed the support of the" -- did you say legally- or illegally-elected government?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I was talking about how I was putting together resources to set up Hidraflex. I wasn't talking about the support, be it legal or illegal. At the time when we were looking for a plot of land where to build the factory, and I wrote to the municipality of Prijedor because they were authorised by the Executive Board to put up certain plots of land for sale. That is to allow Hidraflex to build its factory there, and I addressed the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor. And as -- and I asked to meet the mayor of the municipality, the municipal mayor, on several occasions. But I asked for that, yet we were not fortunate enough to meet and discuss it. That is what I said yesterday. I never mentioned any legal or illegal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let me read a little further in your answer, and perhaps we can see if that refreshes your recollection. Again, the question in the transcript is whether you used the word legally-elected or illegally-elected. You said: "While I was still down there, I enjoyed the support of the -- legally or -- illegally-elected government. I only requested to keep on working normally. When there was a changeover in Prijedor, when one government left, one government arrived. And now I'm speaking about the Serbian government. I ran into significant problems because of the new government, and I am convinced of what I am saying was much more radical than the previous one." So when you're talking about this changeover in Prijedor when one government left and one left arrived, would I correct if I assumed you're talking about the change from Dr. Stakic's government to Mr. Kurnoga's government?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is when I meant. I was not saying whether it was legal or illegal. I simply said that when the new authority took over in the municipality of Prijedor - that is what I called them - that problems started. I considered them opposition, but I also saw them from time to time. I also said that yesterday. So that authority, yes, caused me a lot of trouble. So yes, I was meaning Mr. Kurnoga's cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, if you could perhaps move your chair a little bit closer to the microphone. The interpreters are having a bit of trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, would you consider or did you consider in 1992 Dr. Stakic's government to be legally elected or more legitimate than the government of Mr. Kurnoga? Was that a perception that many individuals in Prijedor had because Dr. Stakic had been elected in the 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not think that. Both governments were elected lawfully as far as I can gather. I have nothing against any government. All I said was that I had certain trouble with the other government, and I spoke about them yesterday. But otherwise both of them, to my mind, were elected lawfully if they were elected by the councilmen in the municipality. How that came about, I don't know, and it was none of my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, as a citizen of Prijedor, who elected -- who do you believe elected Milomir Stakic to be the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The councilmen, the assemblymen at the session of the Municipal Assembly as I know. That is, they voted to place their trust in them. I was never a member so that I cannot really explain it to you precisely, but I think that is how they elected him. And Mr. Kurnoga's government was also I think elected by the majority vote. I think that was the same thing. And I said that to my mind, both governments were elected lawfully except that I had certain problems with the latter government. And yesterday, I explained which problems -- what kind of problems they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And both of those governments were elected by an assembly that only included representatives of the Serbian people. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on. Sir, when you talked about the changeover of governments from Dr. Stakic's to Mr. Kurnoga's government, on page 70 in answer to one of His Honour Judge Schomburg's question, on line 4 you said: "Yes, I said the radical group. The people had been in power before them I think were moderate. Those people who had been before them tried to deal with the economy to do something about it, and the new people that replaced them were radical people. They wanted power at all costs." So would it be correct the difference you saw between the two groups in their policies was how they dealt with the economy, and that's why you labelled one group more radical -- or radical and the other group moderate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in a way, I burnt my fingers with the second government, and I know -- well it was some time ago so I know what happened. And I stand by what I said 100 per cent and I said what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You said on page 68 of yesterday's transcript, beginning on line 15, I'll read in several lines: "Yes, I do know about that. That group, and I think I am well-placed to know it, because that was more my concern than his, that was the opposition who told me even before they came to power that they would take my factory away from me. They tried, but they failed. They had Dr. Stakic removed. I think the chief of the SUP was also removed at that time. People from the municipality were removed, and they appointed their own people." My question is: The chief of the SUP who was removed at the same time as Dr. Stakic was Simo Drljaca. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, but I'd like to make a correction. He was removed from his position from what I heard, from what I knew, from the position of the chief of SUP, that is, the Secretariat of the Interior. I think he left, but I believe he was promoted. He became an assistant minister, and his office was in Bijeljina as far as I know. As far as I know, and I think that I know it. And Dr. Stakic, I think I said that yesterday, too, from what I know was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let me read again the words you used yesterday and you tell me if they are accurate or not. "They had Dr. Stakic removed. I think the chief of the SUP was also removed at that time." Is that correct, or do you now feel that you have to change that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was talking about the municipality of Prijedor that Dr. Stakic was dismissed, but he wasn't the only one. The whole government in the Prijedor Municipality changed. I would merely like to add to it. I don't want to change my statement, but I wish to add to it that Mr. Simo Drljaca was appointed Assistant Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: At the same time that Dr. Stakic and Drljaca were removed, Mr. Kuruzovic -- excuse me, Dr. Kovacevic was removed as president of the Executive Board. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said all of them. A new government, a new group of people took over from the president of the Executive Board to the mayor of the municipality, secretariat of economy, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And the secretary of the economy would have been Mr. Travar. He was replaced at that time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I'm not quite sure. I think he was replaced. I think that at the time when the change took place, that they were -- that they all lost their offices. But once again, I repeat, I wasn't really into politics, and I wasn't much interested in that. But since I was in the town all the time, I was there, I heard, and I heard quite a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, and you also told us in the answer I've just read that you were in a position to know. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, I moved around. I was at work. I was in restaurants. And I repeat it once again, you can learn everything in a small town. Now what of it is true and what isn't is up to everybody to weigh, both -- every side. What I'm saying now, and I believe you are aware of it, is what 90 per cent of the population knew, because it was no secret. But Radio Prijedor also broadcast programmes about it. Kozarski Vjesnik wrote about it. So it was quite regular, and I could learn and hear all these things, if from no other source than from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you did follow the media, Radio Prijedor and Kozarski Vjesnik, during that time period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Yes. I followed as much as my work allowed me because I also travelled a great deal, so that I wasn't always there. Our paper was a weekly, I think, I believe it was on Fridays that it came out, a couple of times there were problems with this publication because the paper was not available. But I followed it, yes, I read it when I had time to do that and when I was in our town. That is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, in 1992, you were one of the economic elite in Prijedor; isn't that correct? You managed an important factory, the Hidraflex factory. You were a partner in a gas station during a time when petroleum products were extremely valuable and in short supply, and you were a person who even travelled abroad during times when any travel was extremely difficult. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you sent your wife to Belgrade, and I'm a little confused about the time. Can you tell us when it was you sent your wife and family to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my wife and children were in Belgrade as of 1990. I had found a private apartment for them, but they also came to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Were you the only Serb as far as you know who sent his family out of Bosnia and Herzegovina during this time period? Or were there other Serbs -- well, first, excuse me because the record. I haven't established that fact. I think no one has asked you. Sir, is your ethnicity -- did you consider yourself -- do you consider yourself a Serb?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Were you the only person of Serbian ethnicity to send his family outside of Prijedor and outside of Bosnia during that time period, or was that something that other people also did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really give you any name right now. But I do know that whoever could do it did it. Some for economic reasons, and of course we have to speak about specific years. If somebody did it in 1992, when these things were happening in those territories in the former Yugoslavia, then I suppose there were people like that. But as I mentioned yesterday, I'm a man -- I was a man who was married with two small children, and I had to decide where to make my life in 1992. I had no other reason for that. I simply wanted to live in a big -- in a proper city so that my children could have something that perhaps I did not have, and I was able to offer it to them. So that was the chief reason. But then things happened, and so they stayed in Belgrade. They still live there. My children were small then. Now my son is 17 and my daughter 15. And they have been attending Belgrade schools from day one. So I had made my plans before everything. Whether people were leaving in 1992, I suppose that people who had where to go and were able to afford it, yes, I suppose there were people who did likewise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that when you and I believe it's Mr. Popovic were planning on starting this business, a private factory, you needed the approval of the government of Prijedor, and you went to see President Cehajic. Why is it that you went to see the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said, and I repeat it, I said it yesterday and repeat it, I did that because we had applied to the Executive Board or the Municipal Assembly, and the Executive Board did not reply for a few months. And we always applied then -- submitted our requests to the Executive Board. But they did nothing. And then we tried to establish contact with the president of the municipality, with the municipal mayor, to see what was wrong, why nothing was happening because -- and this is something that I forgot to mention yesterday. We were offered to set up companies, being told that everything would be private, but nobody was giving us anything. And we were looking for the plots where to build. We were accommodated in a building before that paying an exorbitant rent, yet we had enough money to build a factory, and that is why we wanted to meet with the mayor of the municipality, with the president of the municipality. But it never took place. And the Executive Board very artfully dodged issuing it at the time when everything was legal. And I told you how it all ended up then, that it was put on the agenda of the Municipal Assembly, and the councilmen then voted for it, and I affirm that a number of councilmen didn't know what they were voting for because it was -- it had been read out to them. I think there were 41 to 45 items on the agenda. The councilmen were already tired. And unfortunately, that's how it is, so they voted just like that. When the president of the municipality found out --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, but my question had dealt only with why you went to see the president of the Municipal Assembly. So there's no necessity to repeat your testimony from yesterday if it does not relate to the question. Would it be correct, then, sir -- thank you. Would it be correct, then, sir, that because of inaction of the Executive Board, you went to see the president of the Municipal Assembly in the hope and in the belief that he could influence the actions of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that was the only reason, yes. Because he could pull some weight, he could have a say with some members of the Executive Board. And the Executive Board, if you want me to explain, the Executive Board - and I know this because I was in all the -- this question because of our case - the Executive Board was made of two --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If I need an explanation of that, I'll ask you. Thank you. Thank you for offering. Sir, your decision, you finally received approval when this item was finally put on the agenda of the Municipal Assembly. Would it be correct that you couldn't get action without someone putting on the agenda the decision that you needed, that that was a key step in obtaining this approval? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without this putting on the agenda, we wouldn't be able to get our factory, that is, we could either be given a negative answer or then a favourable answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall to the best of your recollection now when it was that this land sale was actually approved? Do you know the date of the decision or the date when you received a document approving the sale of the land?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the exact date. We set up this factory in 1991, so it was three months. In September it started running, so it could have -- let me see. May perhaps, thereabouts. Around May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of 1991? I just want to be clear about the year.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Who signed -- do you still have the document that you received with the approval?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it. The owner has it in the factory; Mr. Popovic has all these documents. I wouldn't be able to give you the exact dates. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think the dates you've given are sufficient. Thank you. Do you know who it was that signed this decision? Was it Dr. Kovacevic? Was it the president of the Municipal Assembly Professor Cehajic? Who signed the document you received?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor signed the document. That is, the decision. We received that decision, and then based on that decision, we purchased the building plot. It went via the Executive Board. The decision was made by the Municipal Assembly. I don't know who the signator is, whether it was the president of the Municipal Assembly or the president of the Executive Board. I don't know what the procedure actually looked like, but I really didn't care, as long as we had the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: But it would be correct then that the decision was made by the Municipal Assembly and implemented by the Executive Board. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I think happened. The Municipal Assembly made the decision at one of its regular sessions, and then the decision was made. Who signed it, I don't know, whether it was the president of the Municipal Assembly or the president of the Executive Board. I don't know, and it really didn't matter. I know that everything, all of our activities, went through the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I correct something. Looking back now, I remembered something maybe to make things easier for you. The decision was made at the session of the Municipal Assembly, and then I believe that this decision should have been signed by the president of the Municipal Assembly because the decision was made by the Municipal Assembly. I'm saying that because we did not receive the decision in due time because the president of the Municipal Assembly was embittered with some people who voted in favour, and that is why I think it was signed by the president of the Municipal Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 12223 to 12235. Assembly who at the end of the day had to sign it because the decision had been made. What I'm saying is that the decision did not reach us in due time. It was belated. It took a while for the decision to reach us because of this dispute. I believe that even some deputies were removed, not only because of that case but because of some other cases as well. You can verify that, some deputies who had been sitting in the Municipal Assembly before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification -- explanation. I want to move now to the subject of the petroleum station, petrol station, excuse me, that you were a partner in. First, can you tell us where was that located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The petrol station is across the bridge on the Sana River on the road to Sanski Most and further on to Ljubija. The crossroads closest to the petrol station is the crossroads towards Ljubija and Sanski Most. So the petrol station is on the right-hand side immediately after the bridge across the road from the Prijedor Hotel which is on the corner there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is that street called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt. I think it would be helpful for all of us because we have to mark a number of locations in Prijedor that we have as a basis a map of Prijedor where all these locations can be marked. Unfortunately, I don't know in the moment the exhibit number of the map of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps S14.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: While that's being prepared, sir, was that on Djuro Djakovic Street? I may be minspronouncing it. A crossroad in Tukovi or the road just after you cross the bridge going out of town toward Sanski Most

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the name of the street. It was in the neighbourhood called Tukovi. As soon as you cross the bridge, on the right-hand side, it is one of the exits from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. We'll have a map to show. But I understand. Crossing the bridge that's opposite the Prijedor Hotel in the Tukovi neighbourhood going towards Sanski Most, you would take a right on that first major street. Is that correct, and then you would see the gas station?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do we have another copy that --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- perhaps could be marked?
