I think we shouldn't discuss flour because your work was first of all on petrol and derivatives of petrol. So no doubt, you saw these vouchers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see those vouchers. I only heard that vouchers were being distributed. I am just talking about the things that I heard, and I knew where it took place. It took place in Cirkin Polje. There was a Crisis Staff there. Mr. Kuruzovic, Slobodan, was the head of that Crisis Staff. And from there, people would bring flour, sugar, cigarettes, and stuff like that. I never went there to take anything. I didn't need to do that. I only heard that vouchers were being distributed, and then I saw long lines of vehicles at the Energopetrol station. When you look from the direction of Banja Luka at the entrance of Prijedor or the exit from Prijedor, the main road, it is some 150 metres from the crossroads. That's where I saw the long lines of vehicles of people with vouchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are anticipating my questions. Could you please be so kind and mark the building where these vouchers were distributed by the Crisis Staff, once again, with a green marker. I think the next would be number 4.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was this a building especially for the purposes of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, at that moment. Before that, it used to house a company based in Slovenia. I think I've already told you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You told us. I only wanted to put it to you --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Was there any insignia on this building, or was there any name on this building, for example, "Crisis Staff" or insignia for the one or other group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anything like that. I would pass by in the car, but I didn't see any inscriptions on the building. I didn't see anything that would say the Crisis Staff or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You mentioned the same page, line 21, that you often saw Slobodan Kuruzovic there. Did you only pass by or did you enter the house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't enter the house. I didn't need to. I told you where I lived for a few months. So I had to pass. I had to take that road. It was Milan Vrhovac Street, I don't remember the number. Close to the Crisis Staff on the right-hand side is the road where I used to live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was this the only building of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. The only building of that Crisis Staff? Was that the only building that have Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that there were a number of Crisis Staffs in companies. I believe that it was the Crisis Staff of that particular local commune because every local commune had a Crisis Staff which was housed in a building of the local commune. So every local commune had a Crisis Staff. Almost every company had a Crisis Staff. It was not the Crisis Staff for the territory of Prijedor Municipality. I believe that this was the Crisis Staff of the Cirkin Polje local commune or whatever the name of that local commune was at that time. For example, nobody from Ljubija could come to that particular Crisis Staff to obtain petrol vouchers. It was impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to come back to your yesterday's testimony. You mentioned: "I would often see Mr. Slobodan Kuruzovic there." Apparently, based on your testimony some minutes ago, only when passing this building. Now apparently it's your testimony that this --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- This building way tailor-made for Cirkin Polje. Yesterday on page 51, line 21, you added: "I think Mr. Slobodan Kuruzovic was the head of that Crisis Staff." The head of the Crisis Staff of Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, Cirkin Polje. That's where I resided, and I heard from my neighbours that people went there to get cigarettes, to get petrol vouchers, and they told me that Slobodan Kuruzovic was the main person of that Crisis Staff. I believe at the time that it was the Crisis Staff for the Cirkin Polje local commune. In my own village, there was also a Crisis Staff for that village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are coming closer. Where would the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality meet?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be logical that they would meet in the municipal building. I don't know. I never went to any Crisis Staff, either to a Crisis Staff of a local commune or to the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor municipality. But it would be logical that if they were the Crisis Staff of the municipality, that they would meet in the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the head of that Crisis Staff was Dr. Stakic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard, that Dr. Stakic was the head of the Crisis Staff of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So "that's what I heard." Is it really your testimony that you never discussed with Dr. Stakic his capacity as, in this case, head of the Crisis Staff? Do you really want us make believe that you never discussed with Dr. Stakic that he was the head of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. I was not interested in a single Crisis Staff because there is no single Crisis Staff that could help me in my business, in what I did. I believe that Crisis Staffs were dealing with problems in the local community, such as water supply, electricity supply, which was a big problem in Prijedor, and the supply of food-stuff to the town. That's what it was. I never received a request from any Crisis Staff, nor did I ask for anything from a Crisis Staff. It was the same as the Crisis Staff in Cirkin Polje. They just distributed vouchers for petrol and flour and sugar. What would I have to do with them? I didn't need them. That's why I never discussed that with him. And believe me when I told you that I had socialised with him. Don't take that very literally. I didn't socialise with him to benefit from that friendship. I socialised with him because I needed to spend my leisure time with somebody. Everybody needs rest from time to time, and whenever we had time, we would socialise. But we socialised around sports, not around work or politics. I also told you that the president of the Municipal Assembly has never been in the position to help me in any way. And Dr. Stakic was no exception. And that's why I never asked for any special favours from him, especially not in the conditions of war that prevailed at that time. I tried to protect myself in every possible way. I never got involved in any dodgey business, so I never sought any protection from the president of the Municipal Assembly. I didn't need to ask any favours. I didn't need to ask any assistance from him or the MUP or anybody. I wasn't interested in those things. I lived my life. I worked as much as I could. I had enough of my own problems, and I informed you about these problems in the course of the past two days. And what else can I say? That was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You have never been in the basement of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How many competitors did you have in Prijedor as an owner of a petrol station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean other petrol stations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a petrol station towards Kozarac. There was a petrol station there. All the Energopetrol stations operated. They also supplied people with petrol. From time to time, they would have shortages. It depended very largely on the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please mark with a green 6 the location of Energopetrol on the Banjacka Road. You mentioned this yesterday in your testimony, page 50, line 15/16.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't see the crossroads or the entrance to the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is marked as number 5. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 5, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other petrol stations in Prijedor of importance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was another Energopetrol station at the bus terminal and at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please mark the bus terminal as number 6.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever sell fuel to Sanatrans?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. I don't know. My petrol station was open to the general public. Everybody could go there and buy petrol. I don't know whether this particular agency used my petrol station to refuel their cars. There were different vehicles that came, and whoever came could buy petrol. I don't remember. There were a number of buses and other vehicles who came to my petrol station to get fuel. But I wasn't there all the time like I've told you already. And that would be that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But in your petrol station, one would not need vouchers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Opposed to other petrol stations where you would need these vouchers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that private petrol stations and state-owned stations sold fuel for cash. I know that at the Jugopetrol petrol stations that I know from stories, that they issued it for vouchers. But at my pump, that was not allowed. You had to pay cash, and I think that other private petrol stations also sold it only for cash. What vouchers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I come back to your answer of today on page 63, line 10. "I don't know, but my obligation was to give money for all the vouchers that I received." Can you please describe us this voucher. By whom were they issued?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say once again, there was a misunderstanding. At my petrol station, only twice was the subsidized oil distributed, that is, the oil or diesel which I had received through the Executive Board from the commodity stocks reserves of the republic. And then I was given lists. I can't say it was a proper voucher or a list. It looks like a bank note with the name of the person, the quantity to be issued, and there was a stamp of the Executive Board there. But that happened only when the Executive Board decided to distribute this oil. So I wasn't doing it for voucher when we talk about the Executive Board's vouchers. Now, all I had to do -- the Executive Board had organised this campaign for sowing and harvesting because -- I mean, that oil cost 50 and 55 pfennigs, and they subsidized the difference. So a person who came to buy this diesel oil had to pay 50 or -- that is 55 pfennig, and the rest was subsidized by the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to repeat. It was you mentioning today "giving money for all those vouchers." Could you describe us these vouchers? Who issued these vouchers? You yourself mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying, since the diesel, the fuel that reach the petrol station was not property, it was the property of the republican commodity reserves, and we were bound to pay the money to the republic. If we had issued 10 tonnes at 50 pfennigs, then we had to pay into their account 50.000 marks. And the fuel that I issued, I could do that only if I accompanied the bills with these vouchers. But these vouchers, these certificates or whatever, were typed on a typewriter from an individual who came, and they had the full name of that person and the number of litres. And if it said 50 litres, I could issue -- I could give that man only 50 litres, collect the cash from him. But then I had to pay the state for that quantity of fuel. So it was based on the decision of the Executive Board which was then sent to all local communities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm awfully sorry if we don't understand each other. My only question was when this was an official voucher, a voucher or certificate, whatever you want to call it now, it was issued by whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Executive Board. The Executive Board then sent -- had those vouchers done, sent them to local communities. And the secretary of the local community had to account for these vouchers to the Executive Board. That is, say that he had distributed them. And we, if we had a tank of 100 tonnes of fuel, we had these vouchers or certificates or receipts or whatever, we had to account for that. But they came from the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again. We are coming closer. They came from the Executive Board. Could you read the words "Crisis Staff" on these vouchers or certificates? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The Executive Board of the assembly of the municipality of Prijedor, the full name. I told you what it said, the stamp, and the number of litres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I only want to -- that there is no misunderstanding, I am just discussing the period of time as from the beginning of May until the end of December 1992. Could one read on these documents the words "Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. My documents didn't. I told you where one could see it. One could see it if the Crisis Staff distributed vouchers to people, then it had to say the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly. If they were the ones who distributed such vouchers. But such vouchers did not reach me nor did anybody intercede on anybody's behalf. I'm telling you once again, people bringing those vouchers or whatever you care to call them intended for farming, and people came from local communities without that Crisis Staff. It only said Executive Board, Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, and then the full name of the person, and the number of litres that one was entitled to buy at 50 pfennig a litre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What was the car you drove at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a Mercedes 123, an older Mercedes 123, 12, 13 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When you had to refuel your car, where did you go to get the fuel?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When it was necessary to refuel your Mercedes, where did you buy the necessary petrol for your car?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my petrol station, at my petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you never needed a voucher?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But the rest of the population did not need vouchers. The petrol station was open, and everybody could buy fuel without any vouchers. I said it was a campaign meant for agricultural works, and it lasted for three or four days only. Apart from that, it was sold freely, the fuel at my petrol station and everybody came. And of course I had my fuel. Of course, not everybody who came to the petrol station came with a voucher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Opposed to, for example, Energopetrol station on the Banjacka Road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Energopetrol station was no different from my station because they sold the same kind of fuel to the citizenry, and one knows the prices were standardised, uniform. And they were also selling it regularly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I put to you your answer yesterday, page 50, line 15. "Yes, the Energopetrol station on the Banjacka Road where vouchers could be used to obtain petrol. It was a state-owned petrol station. It was the only place as far as I know where you could get petrol for vouchers." This was a different kind of petrol station opposed to yours, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, up to a point, but perhaps we were again talking at crosspurposes. I'm saying that the petrol station received vouchers from that Crisis Staff for the fuel. So I said that the difference, you could not come to our station to tank it. But at other petrol station, apart from the vouchers, also sold fuel to other citizens. But those who came -- the bearers of vouchers could get the fuel without money. I am quite clear about that so I cannot make a mistake and say that this was this way or the other way. So that is what you could do. I think Jugopetrol station, you could tank that fuel for the vouchures, buy that petrol on the free market, when they had it, of course, they didn't have it always. And at my station, you could tank the fuel apart from what I distributed during the agricultural campaign. That is, at my petrol station, you could get fuel for cash only. There was no vouchers or anything apart from these vouchers that I said which were intended for the sowing and harvesting campaign.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you distribute fuel for Autotransport Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was selling it to Autotransport. I worked with them. But we worked through the -- through our bank account. They did not pay cash. They would pay to the bank a certain amount of money for a certain quantity. And that was that. And at certain times they would order me to take a whole truck tanker to their vehicle depot which is at [indiscernable], their depot is there. And I think they called us two or three times in three years' time. Between 1992 and 1995, I think they bought two or three tankerfuls which we would then drive to their vehicle depot. And at times they would also do a favour to us with their tankers, but of course they would charge us for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Normal give and take. To the best of your recollection, when was the first time that you provided Autotransport Prijedor with fuel in this -- how did you call it, sometimes two or three tankerfuls. When was it the first time you sold a tankerful for Autotransport Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was in late 1992, and that before that, they would buy it only as the buses would come along. Towards the end of 1992 or perhaps January 1993, I think that was the first time that we sent them a tankerfull of fuel. They asked for it because they had to pay for it. And it was their tanker which was used, so we simply deducted the price of the transport but filled it. And they also took off fuel to fill in buses. I don't know, of course, whether they would stop at other petrol stations. They had a number of buses and trucks, so I presume they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please understand for our case, we are interested only in this special period of time, beginning of May until the end of September 1992. When was it the first time that a bus of Autotransport Prijedor was refuelled in your station, that Autotransport Prijedor became your customer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometime around July or August. It was summertime. July, August. I can't pinpoint the date. I know it was summer. It was the summer of 1992. Therefore, July or August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you call Autotransport Prijedor as one of your good or excellent customers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. One of the better, but not the best. The best were the citizens since businesses were not particularly well off, those transport trucks -- shipping companies and transport companies who worked, and Autotransport was the only one such company passes the petrol station. It is a good location, at the crossroads leading in various directions. The citizens were actually taking more fuel than Autotransport. And also, the iron ore mine, they had their own buses which were -- which commuted to the mine and from the mine, and also served -- and also transported citizens between Ljubija and Prijedor. They also bought fuel from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did they pay in cash? I think you mentioned it already, but to be on the safe side, or was there any special bank account with Autotransport Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, they paid through a bank account. They are also a public company. They had money on their account. At times, they wouldn't have any money there for about five or ten days. But we would then wait for it, wait, it would be a loan to them. But they paid regularly. There were not any particular payments, and the price was the regular one, as if -- as when you buy petrol at the petrol station less, of course, the amount when their tanker would transport our oil. So we would deduct the price of transportation from the complete -- from the total price.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you know for which purposes the buses of Autotransport Prijedor were used in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To transport passengers, buses. As far as I know, they travelled to Prijedor, Dubica; Prijedor, Novi Grad; Prijedor, Banja Luka; Prijedor, Omarska; Prijedor, Ljubija. Those were the itineraries. Perhaps -- no, not perhaps, but I'm sure that the number of rides was cut shorter as against the situation -- before the situation that occurred because earlier, there were buses leaving Prijedor in all directions every 30 minutes. But that was cut shorter. That was reduced to the minimum. I know that by the fuel they consumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that these buses were used to bring voluntarily or unvoluntarily persons from Prijedor out of the area of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've already mentioned. I already said yesterday in my statement that I took a family out, that is, took them into my home and told them they could stay at my place. They didn't have to go, and nobody would harm them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This wasn't my question. May I ask you to answer my question. My question was related to the buses only. To the buses of Autotransport Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was about to explain that. When I took that family out, I saw two Autotransport buses. And I can't claim this with certainty, those were people who wanted to leave, and those buses went to Novska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you refuel cars of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you refuel --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did -- I'm sorry. Once they had paid in advance, I think it was 550 litres, I don't remember, but this was paid. So yes, I did give fuel for the police cars, that is, during the time that I worked with the petrol station, I sold them 550 litres, which were paid in advance. And that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it lasted until about the new year, between August and the new year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]...

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gave them the fuel, and it lasted for three or four months. That is how long it took them to use up all that fuel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you provide cars of the army with fuel?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not sell any fuel to army vehicles that were not buying it from me or from what I know from other petrol stations as well. They had their own bases, and they had their own petrol station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Final question on this line: Did you ever sell fuel for the Omarska investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to present to the witness Document S180, and there, issue 24. Before asking a concrete question on this, have you been a reader of the Official Gazette of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Never. May I then ask, please, the witness to be shown S399B, page 2. And ask the witness to read out the third paragraph starting with --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I point this out --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please slow down so the interpreters can follow you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I'm pointing this out because Hidraflex may not be considered abundant property in the sense of the decision to proclaim the abandoned property, the state property, the Official Gazette of Prijedor 3/92. The fact that some property has been abandoned is established by the decision of disposition of the relevant body, and only after that a property may be proclaimed state property. It is likewise --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You need not go in further details. But when asked whether you read the Official Gazette of Prijedor, whether you were a reader of the Official Gazette, you answered three minutes ago "never." Here you are making reference to the Official Gazette of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I say it again, that I never read the Official Gazette. What I wrote, I also had a team of people in my company who did their job. I'm not a lawyer. I had a woman who did that and who did what I had ordered her. But I never read the Official Gazette. I've never read a single issue of the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So may I then ask you whether or not you have ever seen the document that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And there, page --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Page number 39, issue 24.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen it and never had it in my hands. I've never read it, never. I only gave a statement, so I see that this is it, where the army got its fuel supply which means that I was not wrong. But they had their petrol station at the barracks, and where they got the fuel for it from, well, they did not get fuel from me. Who supplied them the fuel, I do not know, nor did we use our tankers to supply them with fuel because they had their own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this second point in this order, who owned this petrol station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, Energopetrol. What I just said. When I spoke about the Crisis Staff in Cirkin Polje, that's the petrol station that I marked with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, then, turn to issue 28. As an expert in this field, could you please comment what is the meaning of this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krajinapetrol, I can't even recall where that petrol station is. Oh, yes, perhaps when the name was changed, when Energopetrol became Krajinapetrol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you please read out --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this. I mean, I've never seen it, and I don't understand it. "Krajinapetrol is prohibited to issue oil without the authorisation of the Crisis Staff. The secretary of the secretariat for economy is made responsible to" -- I don't understand this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please go on reading.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, sure. It says: "Krajinapetrol Prijedor is hereby prohibited from giving, from giving -- from issuing oil without the authorisation of the Crisis Staff. "Item 2, the secretary of the secretariat for economy is hereby tasked with arriving at a uniform price for oil and oil derivatives at the Autonomous Region of Krajina level. "Item 3, this order shall enter force on the day of its adoption date. "10th of June, 1992. President of the Crisis Staff. Milomir Stakic." I've read it, and I still don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your testimony is you never saw this order; you never were aware of the content of this order, especially related to a standard price for oil and oil derivatives at the Autonomous Region of Krajina level? You never heard about this, and you never discussed this with Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then finally turn to issue number 29. Have you ever seen this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to see this line of three orders in an area where apparently you were an expert in the area of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I am not a politician. I am a businessman. I never needed this, nobody ever showed it to me. It is not that I am surprised. I only know what petrol stations had fuel, which were supplying fuel. Some of them were supplying fuel against vouchers. I don't know what this is. Nobody ever asked me at my petrol station to supply fuel to the police or the military. I could supply whoever I wanted to supply. I had my friend and relatives that I had to help. And sometimes I would give them small quantities of fuel without payment. I have never seen this. I repeat, and I state that I have never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you have never seen this before --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Presiding Judge, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you have never seen these documents during the last week?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you see any other document during the last week contained in this issue of the Official Gazette of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything like that. Do you mean during the last week, whether I saw something like that? The answer is no, I didn't. No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You have not seen any issue or any order in this volume of the Prijedor municipal gazette during the last week?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PRASTALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said I didn't. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is a clear answer. And this concludes today's hearing. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow -- wait a minute, before we break. We will stay then adjourned until tomorrow. But first let us hear -- again, I repeat, I invite both parties to inform me as soon as possible when they know the Defence what will be the witness, will the witness be available Thursday, Friday, and what about the statement to be expected from the side of, put it this way, senior counsel of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I understand from Ms. Sutherland that Ms. Korner would like to address you after the witness has finished tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's call it a day. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 4.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of February, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
